course:
Honesty, I believe the issue with this course stems not from the subject itself but rather from the fact that we didn't fully grasp ENG 101-102, which we should have learned earlier. I think this is the reason behind the unsatisfactory responses to essay questions. Additionally, the exam format employed in this course is heavily reliant on rote memorization. While I find this memorization aspect relatively easy, I don't consider it to be effective.
On the other hand, I truly enjoy the topics covered in this course. The selection of books and their sequence is commendable as it allows us to see the interconnectedness of the subjects.
The books and texts were much more interesting than the ones in Hum 111. But sometimes we were given very long readings to finish over a few days which was a lot of workload

The lesson's closed-book exams that include 5-7 works don't improve the students' analytical thinking skills as much as open-book essay writing would. Open-book exams focusing on 1-2 books would be more beneficial, advancing students' skills in supporting their arguments more directly through the text.  Limiting the number of books the students are responsible for would also allow a more in-depth consideration of the texts. Even with "short-essay" questions being asked about 5-7 books in a closed-book exam requires memorization. Changing this examination method would improve the course.

Strongest: We learn a lot, thoroughly. The course not only teaches generally about the topics but it analyzes every book, play and etc. in their context. However, in my opinion, the expectations of the instructors (overall) from the students are not clear in this course.  Furthermore, I don't believe there should be MTs and Finals for this course. Not because of the grades but when the content of the course is taken into consideration the students should be evaluated upon their communication skills more. MTs and Finals only encourage us to memorize certain points and forget the rest. On the other hand, presentations, group projects, or individual projects would encourage the student to polish his/her communication skills AND enhance permanent learning.
